annotations.text:
DIRECTION A · CONTROL ROOM  (leading candidate -> Main)
Dark industrial HMI. 3D viewport + dense right-hand instrument stack: live TCP pose, target inputs, per-joint bars.
Why: domain-authentic and glanceable; reads like a real teach-pendant / SCADA screen.
Tradeoff: heavy and engineer-first; less warm as a portfolio centrepiece.

DIRECTION B · EDITORIAL LIGHT
Bright, spacious product UI. Robot on a clean white stage; pose as a large typographic table; minimal chrome.
Why: modern and polished, signals design taste to recruiters, approachable for non-engineers.
Tradeoff: gives up instrument density and some industrial credibility.

DIRECTION C · ENGINEERING BLUEPRINT
Schematic drawing sheet. Wireframe robot with coordinate axes, dimension lines, per-joint callouts and a CAD-style title block.
Why: unforgettable; foregrounds the kinematics story and engineering depth.
Tradeoff: the blueprint conceit can fight real-time legibility and read more as a poster than a live tool.
